headline: South Asia: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir share top spot in list of world’s 500 most influential Muslims
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir share top spot in list of world’s 500 most influential Muslims.
- Western Russia: Romanian PM condemns Russian attack on three commercial vessels in Black Sea.
- Asia: Top Hamas commander killed in Israeli strike in Gaza.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: We’ve broken the glass ceiling, but have we overcome? – Luz Longsworth.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 20 hours ago: We’ve broken the glass ceiling, but have we overcome? – Luz Longsworth.
WESTERN BUREAU: Women have shattered glass ceilings, claimed executive offices, and risen to the highest levels of leadership. But Dr Luz Longsworth is challenging the notion that reaching the top means the battle is won. “We have broken a lot of ceilings, but we have not overcome,” the veteran academic and corporate leader declared last Wednesday evening, warning that women’s growing presence in powerful positions should not be mistaken for the disappearance of barriers to their success. “Don’t let our firsts be our lasts,” she urged.

Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

- Ukrainska Pravda, 12 hours ago: Romanian PM condemns Russian attack on three commercial vessels in Black Sea.
Romanian PM Luca Niculescu has warned of worsening Black Sea security caused by Russia's war against Ukraine following drone strikes on vessels, including the Greek-flagged tanker Evia Petrol V near the Danube Delta.
- The Moscow Times, 14 hours ago: At Least 1 Killed as Ukraine Strikes Industrial Sites Across Russia.
Ukraine’s military claimed responsibility for strikes in Tatarstan, saying it had targeted the Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical complex.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 12 hours ago: Russians strike Odesa, damaging civilian infrastructure.
Odesa authorities have confirmed that civilian infrastructure across the region – including grain warehouses and a car dealership in Odesa – was destroyed in fires caused by a Russian attack on 15 November.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 14 hours ago: Ukraine's General Staff also reports strike on Akhtubinsk airfield in Russia and drone launch site.
Ukraine's General Staff says a strike on Russia's Akhtubinsk airfield caused a secondary detonation at a missile kit depot, and a drone launch site in Oryol Oblast was hit.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Romania slams ‘unacceptable’ drone strikes on Black Sea ships.
- Politico Europe, 13 hours ago: Romania slams ‘unacceptable’ drone strikes on Black Sea ships.
Three commercial vessels were hit near Romania’s coast, prompting fighter jet deployments and fresh calls for NATO support to strengthen Black Sea security.
- Politico Europe, 23 hours ago: Ukraine claims thousands of Russian casualties and a slowing Kremlin advance.
Ukraine is countering Russia's narrative of battlefield success by blunting the Kremlin's attacks.

- Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Pope urges end to Amazon deforestation.
Pope Leo XIV warns deforestation and illegal mining are threatening the Amazon rainforest and the local communities.

- Africanews, 11 hours ago: Daily life in Sudan paralysed by deepening fuel crisis and rising costs.
Domestic refining has been crippled by the civil war while the Middle East conflict has led to significant fluctuations in oil prices.

About 40 schools in the province have reported cases of Ebola since classes resumed in September, with one teacher dying of the disease.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir share top spot in list of world’s 500 most influential Muslims.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 15 hours ago: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir share top spot in list of world’s 500 most influential Muslims.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir have shared the top spot in the latest edition of the world’s 500 most influential Muslims, alongside the Saudi king and crown prince and the Turkish president. The rankings have been compiled by the Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre (RISSC), a research institute based in Amman, Jordan. It has been publishing an annual report titled “The 500 Most Influential Muslims” since 2009, recognising and highlighting individuals who have made significant contributions to Muslim communities.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 15 hours ago: Blasts rattle Bahrain as Iran launches second drone attack in 3 days.
Blasts echoed over Bahrain on Sunday as the tiny Gulf nation was rattled by the second Iranian drone attack in three days, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East war. Sirens rang out, and authorities posted several alerts on social media urging residents to seek shelter, their first warnings since September. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they carried out a drone attack on a US radar system in the desert island state, which hosts US military facilities including a major naval base.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: Authorities ban gatherings in five districts of KP for 30 days, citing law and order situation.
BANNU/BAJAUR/LAKKI MARWAT/SWABI: The district administrations of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bannu, Bajaur, Lakki Marwat, Swabi and Tank on Sunday imposed Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) for a month, banning public gatherings and several other activities amid the prevailing law and order situation. Three of the five districts — Bannu, Bajaur and Tank — are among the 12 districts that were deemed to face intense security challenges and special emergency measures were imposed there.
- The Hindu - International, 19 hours ago: Saudi-led coalition intercepts missiles towards Riyadh, drones in Eastern Province.

- South China Morning Post - China, Politico Europe, 14 hours ago: Top Hamas commander killed in Israeli strike in Gaza.
Hamas said on Sunday that a senior commander who helped plan and oversee the October 7, 2023, attack on Israel had been killed in an Israeli air strike, with the Israeli ‌military confirming his death. Samir Abu Younis, 53, the commander of the Rafah brigade, was killed on Saturday, said the Palestinian militant group’s armed wing, the Al-Qassam Brigades. The Israeli military said it had killed Abu Younis in a strike in the southern Gaza Strip overnight, ⁠adding that he had led the Rafah brigade...
- South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 6 hours ago: Jordan sentences 3 men to death over deadly church attack.
A Jordanian court on Sunday sentenced three men to death by hanging over a deadly church shooting, as the kingdom’s Christmas celebrations were cancelled in solidarity with the victims’ families. Gunmen killed nine people and wounded 25 others when they stormed a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in southern Hammoud village, Karak governorate, on October 23. Authorities said three men, two Jordanian brothers and their relative by marriage, had fled after the attack and were arrested three days...
- South China Morning Post - China, 8 hours ago: Zelensky warns Starshield limits weaken Ukraine defences against aerial attacks.
Restrictions on Ukraine’s Starshield satellite communications system are hindering its ability to intercept Russian drones, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Sunday. He warned that limitations on the system, operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, could weaken defences around Ukraine’s energy infrastructure ahead of the winter months, when Moscow has repeatedly targeted the power grid. Ukraine’s interceptor drones continue to lose contact with their operators when flying faster than 161km/h (100mph)...
- South China Morning Post - China, 13 hours ago: Chinese J-10C fighter spotted carrying modified Russian-origin heavy-strike missile.
New state media footage has surfaced showing for the first time what appears to be a Chinese-modified variant of the Russian-origin Kh-29T air-to-surface missile mounted on a J-10C fighter jet. State broadcaster CCTV’s social media account posted a video on Wednesday featuring Chinese fighters, showing the missile mounted under the 4.5-generation fighter as it took off, according to posts by Chinese military bloggers over the weekend. China originally imported about 2,000 Kh-29T missiles...
India - bottom line: 'Not Cuba or Venezuela': Iran warns it will not wait for US attack before responding.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: 'Not Cuba or Venezuela': Iran warns it will not wait for US attack before responding.
Iran has expressed that it is ready for potential military action while discussing diplomatic avenues with the United States. Deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi indicated three possible scenarios: diplomatic talks, economic blockades, and military response. Tehran has set specific conditions, including ending the war and lifting economic sanctions for any agreement. The arrival of the USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East adds to ongoing regional tensions.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 8 hours ago: Cong suggests Army ‘friendly fire’ behind deaths of 2 SPOs in Kishtwar, BJP hits back.
In Jammu and Kashmir, Congress has called for a thorough investigation into the tragic killing of two special police officers. Initial reports indicate that the officers may have been accidentally shot by Army personnel during a hunting operation. The BJP has dismissed these allegations, claiming they tarnish the integrity of the security forces.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 9 hours ago: Massive Anti-Terrorist Operation Launched In Kashmir Over Kulgam Attack.
The Jammu and Kashmir police, the Army and the CRPF have jointly launched the operation. Top police officers, including J&K DGP Nalin Parvati and the Inspector General of Kashmir Zone, Sujit Kumar, are personally supervising the operation.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 9 hours ago: 'Kisi ke baap ka Hindustan thodi hai’: Diljit Dosanjh takes stage despite threats.
Despite facing threats and considerable opposition, Diljit Dosanjh took the stage in Indore to celebrate culture with his loyal fans. His performance included powerful couplets that highlighted resilience and strength, emphasizing that nothing would deter them from their cherished traditions. Although some emails threatened bomb blasts, authorities later confirmed them as hoaxes. Dosanjh's unwavering dedication showcased his commitment to his audience amidst adversity.

The Alfred hospital in Melbourne confirmed on Monday the independent MP had been discharged Independent Australian MP Helen Haines has been discharged from hospital, four weeks after she was allegedly attacked by a man outside her electorate office in regional Victoria and lost both of her legs. The Alfred hospital in Melbourne confirmed on Monday Haines had been discharged, but provided no further detail. Her office has been contacted. Continue reading...
